Line 40 request(): `let K=v?.timeout??IN` (IN = default timeout) feeds _setupTimeout(w,K,...) and the timeout error, so options.timeout overrides the default deadline. query_results.html:408-422 passes { timeout: DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS } as that second arg. Not ignored or rejected (options are not schema-validated).

memory_admin.html:1095-1103 calls app.downloadFile({contents:[...]}, { timeout: DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS }). In the vendored SDK src/sqllens/ui/vendor/app-with-deps.js:78 (class eI), downloadFile(r,i){...return this.request({method:"ui/download-file",params:r},Db,i)} forwards the second argument as request options. The base Protocol.request (line 40) reads `let K=v?.timeout??IN` and uses it in _setupTimeout and the RequestTimeout error, so the timeout option is honoured over the default. Note the widget loads the SDK from the vendor bundle (inlined/vendored); the same bundle is the source of truth.

Vendored bundle src/sqllens/ui/vendor/app-with-deps.js:40 defines enum RequestTimeout=-32001; class Q (McpError) sets this.code=r; the request timeout handler rejects with `new Q(H.RequestTimeout, ...)` (or Q.fromError(H.RequestTimeout,...) for max total timeout), so err.code === -32001 identifies the timeout. query_results.html:384 uses that check. Caveat: if the caller aborts via signal, a non-Q error y is wrapped into Q with RequestTimeout too, still consistent.

memory_admin.html:1079-1080 downloadFailureReason returns 'timed out' when err.code === -32001. The vendored SDK (src/sqllens/ui/vendor/app-with-deps.js:40, imported at memory_admin.html:355) defines RequestTimeout=-32001, builds the timeout rejection with Q.fromError(H.RequestTimeout,'Request timed out',{timeout}), and McpError class Q sets this.code=r. So the assumption holds and the widget relies on it as claimed.

Vendored SDK app-with-deps.js:78 downloadFile sends ui/download-file and parses with schema Db; line 58: Db = object({isError: boolean().optional() described 'True if the download failed (e.g., user cancelled or host denied)'}).passthrough(). So isError is optional boolean; absent ({} or fields omitted) means success. query_results.html:429-433 treats only result.isError === true as cancelled/blocked and everything else (including undefined/{}) as saved. Matches the claim.

memory_admin.html:1110-1115 treats result.isError === true as refusal/cancel and otherwise shows 'Downloaded'. The inlined ext-apps SDK (src/sqllens/ui/vendor/app-with-deps.js:58) defines the ui/download-file result schema Db = object({isError: boolean().optional().describe('True if the download failed (e.g., user cancelled or host denied).')}).passthrough(), and downloadFile (line 78) parses responses with Db. So the assumption matches the schema; the code's strict === true is consistent with an optional boolean.

Schema half verified: vendored app-with-deps.js line 40/77 defines ui/download-file params as contents: array(union(rb, nb)) with embedded resource uri as plain string D() (no scheme constraint), so file:///query_results.csv is accepted (the only startsWith("file://") is the unrelated roots/list schema). The code at query_results.html:414 sends that URI (diff.patch:220 -> 229). But the 'hosts derive the saved filename from it' half depends on external host behavior (e.g. Claude Desktop) which is not in the repo; no source here shows how hosts derive filenames. Missing evidence: host implementation or ext-apps spec text on filename derivation.

memory_admin.html:1099 builds uri "file:///" + filename; the export handler sets filename = "memory-export." + resolvedFormat (line 1196), giving file:///memory-export.json or .csv. The vendored SDK schema (app-with-deps.js:77) for ui/download-file takes contents as an array of embedded or linked MCP resources, so the request shape is valid and the URI is well formed. The same convention is used by the existing query_results.html:414 (file:///query_results.csv). Whether a host accepts that URI and derives the filename from it is host-side behavior. No host implementation or spec text in the supplied views settles it, so I could not verify it. I did not run a host.

criteria.json read and counts (criterion 3 matches). memory_admin.html:1109-1117: when downloadFile resolves and result.isError === true, calls showError('Export not saved', 'Download cancelled or blocked by the host.' + warningsTail) (red errbar, memory_admin.html:470) and returns before any clipboard/overlay/showOk code (1119+). query_results.html:428-434: same condition calls flashMeta('Download cancelled or blocked by the host.' + warningTail) and returns; no 'Downloaded' message, no clipboard write, no overlay. Split condition `!thrown` / `result && result.isError === true`: alternatives -> thrown (sets thrown=true, goes to clipboard cascade) = outside the trigger (trigger is a resolved download); result falsy/empty or isError not true -> 'Downloaded ...' = outside the trigger (needs isError: true; covered by sibling criterion 2 'does not have isError: true (an empty result included)'); caps.downloadFile absent -> outside the trigger (requires app.downloadFile to be called).

Split of trigger (caps.downloadFile && throw && copy succeeds): alternatives: writeText success -> matches; writeText fails then execCommand success -> matches, same string; non-throw paths (resolved result/isError) -> outside the trigger (download did not throw; criteria 2/3); no capability -> outside the trigger (criterion 1); both clipboard fail -> overlay, outside the trigger (copy does not succeed; criterion 5). Message-less thrown error falls back to String(err), a minor extension within 'any other thrown error'.

criteria.json has criterion 5 matching this claim. query_results.html:403,426,437,449 and memory_admin.html:1090,1107,1119,1137: the same `reason` variable ("This host can't save files" by default, "Download failed (<reason>)" when downloadFile throws) feeds both the clipboard message and the overlay. Overlay hints: query_results.html:327-329 and memory_admin.html:1162 are `reason + " and the clipboard is blocked. Select all and copy:"`. Grep of src finds no "Host blocked the file download". Each overlay function has exactly one caller, which passes reason. Trigger split: overlay is reached only after (no downloadFile cap -> default reason) or (download threw -> Download failed reason), then clipboard.writeText failure and execCommand false. Resolved download paths (isError or success) return before the overlay, so they are outside the trigger because the content never reaches the overlay. Both reasons are covered by the claim. Note: query_results appends the warning after the hint, and memory_admin shows it in a separate line. That is warning placement, not the criterion's hint opening.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} objects and contains criterion 9, so it counts. The diff touches only the two widget files (src/sqllens/ui/query_results.html, src/sqllens/ui/memory_admin.html), docs, a changelog and a new test. It changes no host-side downloadFile support or capability advertisement. Code condition split: `if (caps.downloadFile)` in exportCsv (query_results.html ~L400-425) and offerDownload (memory_admin.html ~L1085-1110). (a) caps.downloadFile falsy -> no downloadFile call and no file; the widget copies to the clipboard with reason "This host can't save files" -> outside the trigger only in the sense that it is the claimed no-file behavior; no departure. (b) result.isError===true -> one message for both cancel and refusal ("Download cancelled or blocked by the host."), which keeps them indistinguishable; no departure. (c) thrown error with code -32001 -> reason "timed out" -> "Download failed (timed out) — ... copied to clipboard"; the request passes {timeout: 600000}, so the timeout is now 10 minutes. Other thrown errors take the "Download failed (<message>)" route, which is outside this criterion's timeout trigger. (d) resolved without isError -> "Downloaded ... ✓"; this is not a departure from the claim. Tests in tests/unit/test_widget_export_outcomes.py cover the nocap, iserror and timeout cases. The repo does not show whether the tenant website chat widget advertises the capability; the claim is conditional ("if it does not") and nothing in the diff changes that host.
